continents/trowen/biomes.title: Biomes
continents/trowen/biomes.content:
Trowen is a cold and lush continent, dotted with sparse settlements, especially towards the East. Trowen is primarily made up of three biomes. East Trowen is split between temperate forests in the North, making up the vast majority of the Bethionese Theocracy and about half of the Trag Empire, and unusually cold jungles in the south, taking up the entirety of Khret and most of Nasesh. West Trowen however is dominated by a giant, and seemingly unnatural, tundra. The upper half of the tundra is controlled by the empire, with the lower half being controlled by the Republic of Vun. No one knows why the tundra formed, though there’s no shortage of speculation.
Forests
The temperate forests of Western Trowen are home to many bizarre arcane sites, frequently blamed, sometimes even correctly, on the many rogue and wandering wizards who use the regions seclusion to conduct bizarre and unethical experiments without interference. In addition to these wizards multiple druidic sects call the region home. These sects are highly isolationist, frequently being unknown and all but forgotten by the world for decades, until loggers choose to chop for wood in the wrong forest. These sects and their beliefs vary wildly, some venerating the balance and harmony of nature, others the savageness of predators. The largest sect, which has multiple settlements through the Bethionese Theocracy venerate Iteus and are widely feared, despite following the same deity as the theocracy. Gentler sects do exist though, with some even opposing the theocracy’s brutal treatment of heretics.
Features and wonders

A stretch of territory said to be home to an immortal silver stag that will grant those that catch it a wish.
A long abandoned cemetery rumored to be haunted, ghastly wails echoing through the trees for miles around.
A pine grove made up of multiple concentric rings of trees, at the center of which is a faerie ring that serves as a portal to the feywild.
A doorway made of twisted vines that hum with latent magic.
An antlered skull the size of a building.
Centered in a clearing dominated by giant purple stalks of vines stands a jet black obelisk inscribed with jagged markings.
A large, ring-shaped tower with no windows or doors. In the center of the ring grows a pure white elm tree.
A spring of lilac-scented fluorescent purple water that bubbles out of the massive stump of an ancient tree.
A seemingly abandoned city of strange spherical buildings built on the cast caps of colossal vibrant blue mushrooms.
A rock formation that looks like a hag. It spawns in a different region of the forest every dawn.
A tree-filled grotto that surrounds a pool where the shed skin of a divine is said to lie.

Jungle
Southern Trowen is home to a truly strange biome, a snowy jungle. Despite the frigid temperatures plants thrive, even those that typically require far warmer temperatures, leading to this region producing most of the continents food. This is largely accepted as an effect of the Flux-wood trees that are only known to grow in this region, mainly in Khret. Plants and animals in this region have been known to spontaneously mutate, usually in beneficial ways, though sometimes in random horrific ways. As a result these jungles are home to life far stranger and more varied than most of the rest of the planet.
Features and wonders

An overgrown temple ruin rumored to have a degree of sentience.
A path that stretches that stretches for miles, lined in faerie lights, that leads to a glade tended by am awakened tree.
An invisible city of the fey high in the canopy.

Tundra
The tundra that dominates western Trowen is without a doubt the continents greatest mystery, and one that scholars have debated for centuries. Based on it’s position on the planet it should be somewhat cold but nowhere near what it is. Over the years hundreds of ideas have been put forth, ranging from it being the result of a wizard circles experiment gone wrong, the divines sealing something beneath the layers of permafrost, and the home of the goddess of ice and snow, Name Needed being hidden somewhere within the vast expanse.
Features and wonders

A hot spring in the middle of a snowy plain where strange, possibly fey, creatures have been seen.
Massive pale yellow crystals stick out of a frozen mountain. Inside the crystals are massive shadowy shapes that sometimes move.
Giant glowing columns of ice stretch high above the landscape. Roaring blue flames burn at the top of each column.
Inside a ring of standing stones, on a frozen plateau, it is always a warm spring day.
An area of the rocky tundra covered with bright pink permafrost. Using this frost in a potion increases its potency.
A large chasm that spews frigid air and icy water in a large plume 100 feet high.
Frozen into the side of a mountain is a sphere that appears to contain a living aurora borealis.

races/gaunts.content:
Sinister, lanky people

Introduction
Gaunts, as the name implies, are lanky humanoids, their rail thin-stature emphasized by their height, standing a full head taller than most humans. Gaunts are widely known for their unsettling appearance, and close ties to Vipkila’s three moons, with it often being said that the moons themselves sent them down to serve as their representatives. There is more truth to this idea than most realize, although not even the gaunts themselves can agree on all the details.
Biology
Gaunts, in addition to being lanky, appear to be blessed with a degree of grace and fluid movement that verges on unnatural, and can often be unsettling to look at. This fact is only made worse by how pronounced their joints are. Adding to this unsettling appearance is the fact they they’re skin ranges from an ash gray to pale ivory, and that they’re naturally completely bald. These traits together have made gaunts draw frequent comparisons to bodies in a morgue. Finally their eyes are universally a pale silver, and far larger than those of an ordinary human.
The most interesting thing about gaunts though is how they seem to draw strength from the moon they’re associated with. This comes with upsides during a full moon, but can be debilitating during a new moon, causing many gaunts to go into seclusion when their moon is new. The exact effects vary based on the gaunt’s associated moon, but it can be generally described:

New Moon: The gaunt grows weaker and more withdrawn. Their voice during this stage will begin to sound raspy, and they may struggle with both focus and memory. Most gaunts will try to isolate themselves during this period to ride it out, trusting their care to gaunts associated with other moons.
Waxing Moon: Gaunts gradually return to their ordinary amount of vitality, and are often overtaken by a feeling of wanderlust, although they don’t travel far.
Full Moon: This is when gaunts are at their strongest and most lucid, their eyes shining far brighter than usual. All gaunts will experience hightened sessions, and some have even recorded extrasensory perceptions, such as being able to see through illusions, and even listen in on the thoughts of others.

Disease Resistant: As a result of the nectar within them lepids can resist all known natural and magical illnesses.

The number of accounts of lepids appearing near battlefield, hospitals and similar locations has begun to draw the attention of scholars, and led to questions about the exact nature of the arch-fey they came from, and why they were slain.

races/lepids.title: Lepids
races/lepids.content:
Butterfly/moth people

A figure staggered forward in a moonlit meadow, drawing ragged and gurgled breaths, and clutching a festering wound at it's side. It looked over it's shoulder, amber eyes darting around in search of it's pursuer, only to be suddenly shocked by another bolt of crackling energy, sending it stumbling to the ground. Looking up, the once immensely powerful being looked into it's attacker's hollow eyes before another bolt of energy brought it's life to an end.
As the attacker looked over the body, ensuring that the job was done, it began to tremble, before blossoming open like a flower, nectar-like golden blood spilling into the meadow, spawning a field of flowers. Seeing this the figure turned and in an instant vanished from the meadow. Soon after, butterflies, drawn by the sickly sweet smell of the blood, came to feed.

Introduction
Lepids are a strange and ancient race, coming into being after butterflies inadvertently fed on the blood of a slain arch-fey, who’s name has been long since lost to time. They’re thought to have held dominion over flowers, blossoming, and the fleeting beauty created by nature; as a result their death poured this power out into the world, where the lepids inadvertently seized it. The field still exists, although it’s location is known only to the oldest and most powerful of the lepids, with the knowledge basically being a death sentence for any other race that tries to find it.
Biology
Lepids are far more different from humanity that simply being “humanoid butterflies” would imply.

At a distance their wings appear to share the same beautiful coloring of a butterflies, but under closer inspection you can tell that they’re made of a semi-transparent fleshy material, with the coloration coming from a patchwork of multicolor veins running through them. These colors can be adjusted by the lepid, and the colors are often used by lepids as a means of communication, rather than spoken language. They can also mimic the speech of other races by vibrating their wings to create specific pitches, although this process doesn’t come naturally to them, meaning most lepids cannot speak to outsiders.
Their bodies are slender and segmented, like those of an insect. They stand about a head shorter than most humans, and have ball like joints, similar to a doll or drawing mannequin. They’re almost entire covered in a thick, porcelain like exoskeleton, though that offers little in the way of physical protection. Their exoskeleton is covered in small, nearly invisible holes that they use for breathing.
Their faces are smooth and mask-like, covered in a featureless layer of the same porcelain like material that covers the rest of their body. They have no visible eyes or mouth, yet are able to see out of the entirety of their face, with it essentially working as a single giant eye, through unknown means. Their lack of a mouth doesn’t impact them as they don’t need to eat, breath through their exoskeleton and “speak” by vibrating their wings to mimic speech. Lepids who frequently deal with members of other races often, such as merchants and diplomats, wear porcelain masks onto of these faces in a- frequently failed- attempt to put others more at ease.
Only one story of a lepid being dissected exists, which asserts that their mostly hollow, with their anatomy mainly consisting of a set of strange kidney like organs forever cycling the essence they drank from the fallen arch-fey eons ago. Most disregard the story, but some more fanciful wizards have theorized that as the arch-fey held dominion over the cycles of growth, blossoming and wilting, lepids may be internally mimicking it, though what this may mean is unknown.
Lepids don’t age in the traditional sense, and outside of when they’re killed by external forces never die. When a lepid reaches 100 years old they’re driven to create a cocoon for themselves. Entering inside the divine blood inside of them breaks through and unmakes them, transforming them into a slurry, before slowly reforming them over the course of a year. The lepid is completely helpless during this process, something made worse by the fact that the slurry they’re reduced to is highly sought after by certain unethical alchemists for it’s extreme regenerative properties, being capable of healing any and all wounds and diseases; even those brought on by curses.
Lepids are also completely infertile, with the only way of creating new lepids being bringing them to original field of flowers the race was born in. This is very rarely done, as the few who know the fields location know how much wizards and scholars long to know it’s location and the lengths they’ll go to in order to seize control of it.

Culture
Lepids, perhaps due to their origin, prize beauty above all else, to the point where their entire society revolves around it. What separates them from many of the other mortal artists spread throughout the world is the fact that they don’t pursue a perfect, eternal form a beauty, instead pouring their time and resources into spectacles they know won’t last. Some pour their effort into growing beautiful flowers that bloom for a single day, some create sand patterns that will be destroyed by high tide, and some others have taken an interest in fireworks, a recent invention they discovered by trading with Ravkin wanderers.
Most Lepid structures are cultivated from magical plants, and begin wilting after only a few weeks, requiring new structures be grown, which is never quite the same as the original. The sole exception is their “Hibernaculum,” where they go to enter their year long cycle of “reblooming.” As a result lepid settlements are constantly changing as layouts slowly change and buildings are repeatedly replaced.
They generally dress in flowy robes adorned with a large array of colors, many of which can only be seen by fellow lepids. Their blacksmithing and craftsmanship is also highly praised, although not for it’s durability or power, with it being fairly standard in those areas, rather for it’s beauty and artisanship. Wealthy members of most major races are known to flaunt lepid crafted goods as a status symbol.

Lepid Traits:
Age: Lepids go through a cycle of death and rebirth. Every hundred years they undergo a year long “reblooming.” Unless killed by outside forces they’re effectively immortal.
Size: Lepids are around five feet tall.
Gliding: Their transformation from butterflies took their ability to fly, but lepids still possess the ability to glide tremendous distances. Their settlements often feature a center spire they can glide from when traveling abroad, to give them a good start.
Eerie: Lepids are often ill received by other races, especially those that know little of them. Their alien appearance, and the strange buzzing their means of speaking produce puts others on guard.
Frail: Lepids are notably frailer than most races, being weaker in terms of strength, and possessing exoskeletons that easily shatter.
Disease Resistant: As a result of the nectar within them lepids can resist all known natural and magical illnesses.

Ravkin Traits:
Age: Ravkin mature at about the same rate as humans for the first 45-50 years of their lives, before their aging slows to a crawl, allowing them to live between 150 and 200 years.
Size: Ravkin are typically below four feet tall.
Heightened Senses: Ravkin have very sensitive hearing and sight, allowing them to both notice small prey at considerable distance, and notice details that others would typically miss (proficiency with perception and investigation).
Carnivorous Nature: Ravkin are obligate carnivores. They don’t eat nearly as much as humans, and typically only need to eat once a day, although they’ll often eat twice a day, once at dawn and once at sunset, when they can.
